classification_definitions.A: EV paper, but the routing model does not model a charging process during the planned operation. This class is excluded from concurrency evidence.
classification_definitions.B: The routing/scheduling model contains charging decisions or charging time, but no finite charger, station-time, queue, or simultaneous-vehicle capacity is imposed; the formulation therefore permits multiple vehicles to use the same physical station concurrently.
classification_definitions.C: The charging process is modeled and a finite concurrency/capacity restriction is imposed through charger resources, station-time capacity, queueing, or an explicit simultaneous-vehicle upper bound.

records.paper: Wu, Lin, Liu & Jin (2022), The multi-depot electric vehicle scheduling problem with power grid characteristics, Transportation Research Part B 155, 322-347
records.page: accepted manuscript pp.11-12, Eqs. (11)-(14); p.23 benchmark construction; pp.30-31 Guangzhou case
records.classification_reason: The time-expanded network represents every station-time window as a charging activity. Eq. (13) bounds the number of buses assigned to activity j by station capacity V_Tj, and Eq. (14) bounds that concurrent count by peak-load variable L. Eq. (12) separately limits depot dispatch capacity.
records.original_evidence: Eq. (13): sum_k sum_i x^k_{ij} <= V_Tj for all charging activities j in T. Eq. (14): the same concurrent charging count <= L. The p.12 explanation says (13) enforces charging-station capacity and (14) the peak-load restriction.
records.depot_side_setup: Buses are fully charged overnight and fast-charge during the day. A station may be located at a terminal or off-route; the benchmark randomly sizes depot and station capacities by instance scale and uses 200 kW. In the Guangzhou case one charging station is located at Guangzhou National Archives Hall, a route terminal/depot location; depot capacity and charging-station capacity are each assumed to be 30 vehicles, fleet size is 100, and fast charging is 30 minutes with power below 200 kW.

ratio_finding: Among the seven papers that genuinely model charging, 5/7 (71.428571%) model charging without finite concurrency and 2/7 (28.571429%) impose finite concurrency/capacity. The one Class A paper is excluded from both numerator and denominator.

depot_side_comparison_to_resetp.basis: Five of seven active-charging papers impose no finite concurrency. Of the two finite-capacity papers, Froger uses one or two chargers per en-route station, so two equals its less restrictive arm; Wu's bus case uses station-time capacity 30. For power, 22 kW equals Montoya's middle curve, is below Wang's 30 kWh/h and far below Wu's up-to-200 kW fast charging, while exceeding Montoya's 11 kW curve. Combining only two concurrent positions with 22 kW therefore places ReSETP on the tight side of the sample's resource-pressure axis.
depot_side_comparison_to_resetp.direct_depot_contract_finding: None of the eight papers reports an observed delivery-depot contract of exactly two chargers at 22 kW each. Most assume full departure energy and leave depot hardware unmodeled; Schneider co-locates an uncapacitated station at the depot; Wang permits depot charging without charger count; Wu supplies the only finite depot/terminal-side scale but for electric buses at 30 vehicles and about 200 kW.
